phonemes.desc: Initial sound of Asía, as attested in the greek-location tradition.
Subsequent syllables preserve the name's inherited shape.

pronunciation.note: Asía is Tier 1 because its Unicode restoration preserves the orthographic signature appropriate to the greek-location tradition.

domains.title: Personified Continent of Asia
domains.subtitle: The domain of Asía
domains.lead: In the greek location tradition, Asía governed personified continent of asia. The name encodes a sphere of power that shaped ritual, narrative, and social order.

cards.title: Primary Sphere
cards.body: Asía is principally associated with personified continent of asia.

cards.title: Cultural Role
cards.body: Worshippers approached Asía through cult, myth, and the material culture of the greek-location world.

symbols.name: Cult site
symbols.meaning: Sanctuary or holy place where Asía was honoured

symbols.name: Ritual object
symbols.meaning: Material focus of devotion for Asía

mythology.lead: The myths of Asía preserve the name's power and personality across generations of retelling.

myths.title: The story of Asía
myths.text: Asía appears in greek location tradition as a figure whose domain over personified continent of asia shapes both cosmic order and human experience. The surviving narratives emphasize Asía's role, attributes, and relationships with other powers.

lore.syncretism: Greek cult and myth travelled with colonists, traders, and conquerors; Roman adaptation, Hellenistic ruler cult, and later European classicism all recast this name for new audiences.
lore.culturalLegacy: The name endures in place names, scholarly vocabulary, modern fiction, and the ongoing recovery of ancient Greek culture through archaeology and philology. Restoring Asía in Unicode preserves the name's cultural specificity against the flattening force of plain ASCII.
lore.extendedMeditation: Names are not merely labels; they are compressed worlds. Asía carries within it a greek location understanding of the eastern continent (possibly from assuwa). Unicode restoration returns that world to readable form.
sources: Homer. Iliad and Odyssey; Hesiod. Theogony and Works and Days.
Beekes, R. S. P. Etymological Dictionary of Greek. Leiden: Brill, 2010.
Material evidence from the Greek world — inscriptions, sanctuaries, votive deposits, and literary papyri — anchors the name in historical cult.
